concept.name: False breakout
concept.definition: A breakout (or breakdown) that fails to hold: price moves beyond a watched level but cannot sustain itself there and closes back inside the prior range. It is the classical-TA label for a failed break; Smart Money Concepts frames the same event as a liquidity sweep.
concept.intuition: Price teases a move out of the box, luring in breakout traders, then snaps back inside — trapping them on the wrong side.
concept.mechanics: Identified only in retrospect: price trades beyond the level, then fails the follow-through test by closing back within the old range. Traders reduce exposure to false breaks by requiring closes beyond the level, volume confirmation, or a successful retest before acting.
concept.failure_modes: The concept is inherently after-the-fact: at the moment of the break, a genuine breakout and a false breakout look identical, so filters that screen out false breaks also delay entry on real ones.
concept.misconceptions: That false breakouts are always deliberate manipulation; the footprint is real, but intent cannot be proven from a chart.
concept.example: ChartSchool's WorldCom example: price briefly poked above 62 resistance in mid-June 1999, then gapped back down days later, nullifying the breakout.
